question: A 40-year-old male presents to his primary care physician for a regularly scheduled check-up. Physical examination reveals nontender cervical lymphadenopathy. A biopsy of the lymph node reveals aggregates of follicular architecture, and cytogenic analysis shows a t(14;18) translocation. The protein most likely responsible for the patient’s condition does which of the following:?

options.opa: Regulates passage through the cell cycle
options.ope: Regulates cell growth through signal transduction

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: t(14;18) translocation -> overexpression of BCL2 -> inhibits apoptosis -> 80% CHAIN: t(14;18) translocation -> BCL2 protein -> inhibits apoptosis -> 85% CHAIN: t(14;18) translocation -> BCL2 protein -> inhibits programmed cell death -> inhibits apoptosis -> 80%
analysis: The presence of a t(14;18) translocation in the biopsy sample indicates a diagnosis of follicular lymphoma, a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. This translocation results in the overexpression of the anti-apoptotic protein BCL-2, which inhibits apoptosis and promotes cell survival.
